committees.name: Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee

dimensions.assessment: Affects federal employees who are relocated in the interest of the government across all federal agencies.
dimensions.evidence: pay to an employee who relocates in the interest of the Government, a one-time lump sum payment

dimensions.assessment: Changes the payout mechanism of relocation expenses from reimbursement to a one-time lump-sum payment for eligible federal employees.
dimensions.evidence: one-time lump sum payment in lieu of any payment otherwise authorized or required under this subchapter

dimensions.assessment: Agencies are directed to collect data on cost savings achieved by the Act and report it to the GSA within 3 years.
dimensions.evidence: Data on cost savings achieved by the Federal Relocation Payment Improvement Act.

dimensions.assessment: Amends title 5, United States Code, requires GSA regulations for implementation, and creates an administrative appeal process.
dimensions.evidence: Administrator of General Services shall prescribe regulations necessary for the implementation and administration of this section

dimensions.assessment: Permanently authorizes the lump-sum relocation authority for all federal agencies.
dimensions.evidence: permanently authorizes all federal agencies to pay employees' relocation expenses using lump-sum payments

missing_information: Exact dollar amounts of cost savings or relocation payments are not specified in the text.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill permanently authorizes all federal agencies to offer lump-sum relocation payments instead of expense reimbursements to federal employees relocated in the interest of the government. It establishes GSA regulations, dispute and appeal processes through the Civilian Board of Contract Appeals, and agency reporting requirements.
